tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to see what AlpacaTradingAgent is: a multi-agent LLM trading research framework built on TradingAgents, where specialized agent teams analyze markets and the resulting decisions can be executed as paper or live trades on Alpaca. ARCHITECTURE.md complements it with the package map, the analysis lifecycle, memory and learning, persistence and testing conventions. Read both first; the remaining steps follow the same lifecycle they describe.

tour.title: Central Configuration
tour.description: Almost every module reads settings from DEFAULT_CONFIG, which defines paths, LLM provider and model choices, debate depth, risk sizing, safety limits, alerts, regime detection, parallelism and context budgets. The dataflows config module holds the active config dict plus runtime API key overrides and typed getters, which is why it ranks among the most depended-on files. env.sample documents the provider and broker credentials that feed this configuration.
tour.languageLesson: A module-level dict as a default config, combined with getter functions that layer environment variables and runtime overrides on top, is a common Python pattern for keeping configuration in one place without a full settings framework.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: The command line is the most direct way to drive a run. cli/main.py is a Typer/Rich application that gathers the user's selections through the interactive questionary prompts in cli/utils.py (ticker, date, analysts, research depth, LLM provider and models), then runs TradingAgentsGraph with a live multi-panel progress display. Following its imports leads straight into the core pipeline in the next step.

tour.title: Graph Orchestration Core
tour.description: TradingAgentsGraph is the heart of the project: it configures LLMs, memories and tools, then runs the LangGraph workflow with checkpoints and audit logging. GraphSetup assembles the StateGraph from analyst, tool, researcher, trader and risk nodes, while the AgentState TypedDicts define the shared state that flows between them. Propagator builds the initial state, and ConditionalLogic decides when analyst tool loops and debates end.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph models an agent workflow as a StateGraph: nodes are functions that read and return partial updates to a shared TypedDict state, and conditional edges are routing functions that pick the next node from the current state.

tour.title: LLM Provider Layer
tour.description: The graph from Step 4 needs language models, and this layer hides provider differences behind one interface. The factory maps a provider name to a client (OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Google, Anthropic or Azure), all deriving from an abstract base client. The OpenAI model registry decides whether a model uses the Responses or chat API and which reasoning and sampling parameters are valid.
tour.languageLesson: An abstract base class with a factory function is the classic Strategy plus Factory combination: callers ask for a client by name and get an object with a uniform interface, so adding a provider does not touch the agent code.

tour.title: External Prompt Templates
tour.description: The prompt loader is the single most imported file in the codebase, because every agent renders its instructions from external Markdown templates instead of hardcoded strings. The templates README explains the folder layout (shared, analysts, researchers, managers, trader, risk, trading modes, graph), the runtime placeholders and the TRADINGAGENTS_PROMPT_DIR override. The loader adds path traversal protection and clear errors for missing placeholders, which keeps prompts editable and auditable.

tour.title: Analysts and Data Tools
tour.description: Analyst agents are the first nodes in the graph, and they gather evidence through tools. The Toolkit in agent_utils exposes LangChain tools for market data, news, fundamentals, macro, FX and crypto, wrapping them with timing, retry and output-quality scoring. Those tools call dataflows/interface.py, which turns Finnhub, Google News, Reddit, stockstats, Alpaca, DefiLlama, macro and other sources into formatted report strings; the market analyst shows how one analyst uses them.
tour.languageLesson: LangChain tools are plain Python functions decorated with @tool; their signature and docstring become the schema the LLM sees, so the model can decide which tool to call and with what arguments.

tour.title: Shared Context and Debate
tour.description: Once analysts finish, their reports go into a shared context: report_context chunks them, extracts scored evidence claims (freshness, numeric support, contradictions) and builds per-agent context bundles within token budgets. The bull and bear researchers debate using this bundle, and the research manager judges the debate, producing a structured ResearchPlan. This adversarial setup is how the framework tries to balance optimistic and pessimistic readings of the same evidence.

tour.title: Trader and Structured Decisions
tour.description: The trader turns the research manager's investment plan, the report context and past memories into a structured TraderProposal. Decisions along the pipeline are Pydantic models (ResearchPlan, TraderProposal, RiskDecision, TradeIntent) defined in schemas.py, and structured.py binds LLMs to these schemas with a free-text fallback. agent_trading_modes adapts prompts and recommendation parsing to investment versus margin trading modes.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic models give LLM output a typed contract: calling an LLM with structured output validates the response against the model's fields, so downstream code works with real objects rather than parsing free text.

tour.title: Risk Debate and Sizing
tour.description: The risk manager adjudicates a debate between aggressive, conservative and neutral debators, emits a RiskDecision and derives a validated TradeIntent from it. Deterministic code then bounds what the LLM proposed: position_sizing combines ATR-based stops, fractional Kelly and exposure caps, the regime detector scales size by volatility, trend and liquidity, and the portfolio layer applies correlation penalties and a gross exposure cap.

tour.title: Safe Execution on Alpaca
tour.description: SignalProcessor turns the final risk decision into an executable action, preferring the typed intent from Step 10. alpaca_utils is the broker adapter: it fetches market data and account state and performs guarded trade execution with risk sizing and bracket protective orders. Before any order, the LLM-free SafetyGuard applies notional and concentration caps, daily-loss and drawdown circuit breakers, a file-based kill switch and a daily token budget, and alerts.py sends notifications when it blocks something.

tour.title: Auditing, Memory and Reflection
tour.description: Every run is auditable: RunAuditLogger writes per-run JSON logs of events, prompts, tool calls, agent outputs and state snapshots with config redaction, and the checkpointer stores per-ticker SQLite LangGraph checkpoints so runs can resume. The memory layer keeps ChromaDB-backed similar-situation memories and a Markdown decision log, and the Reflector compares past decisions with realized returns to write lessons back into each agent's memory.

tour.title: Backtesting Recorded Decisions
tour.description: Because Step 12 persists every decision, the backtest package can replay them. signals.py loads run logs from eval_results and normalizes decisions to BUY, SELL or HOLD; the Backtrader-based engine executes them at next-bar open with slippage and commission, including walk-forward evaluation. metrics.py computes returns, Sharpe, drawdown and win rate, and teach.py feeds forward outcomes back into agent memories without leaking future data.

tour.title: Dash Web UI
tour.description: The web UI is the second front end over the same pipeline. run_webui_dash.py launches the app, app_dash.py builds it and registers every callback module, and layout.py assembles the panels. The global AppState tracks analysis queues, per-symbol agent statuses, reports and tool logs, while components/analysis.py runs TradingAgentsGraph per symbol and can execute the resulting trade intent on Alpaca.
tour.languageLesson: Dash callbacks are Python functions decorated with Input and Output declarations; Dash re-runs them whenever an input component changes, which gives a reactive UI without writing JavaScript.

tour.title: Deployment, CI and API Checks
tour.description: The Dockerfile uses a multi-stage build: dependencies are installed into a venv in a builder stage, and a non-root runtime image serves the Dash UI on port 7860 with a health check. docker-compose binds that port to localhost and persists the data cache, eval results and trading state in named volumes. The GitHub Actions workflow runs the offline pytest suite on Python 3.11 and 3.12 and lints the Postman collections, whose read-only provider checks are described in postman/README.md.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use several FROM statements: the builder stage carries compilers and build tools, and the final stage copies only the installed environment, keeping the runtime image small and reducing its attack surface.
